task.title: Gibwork Developer Hackathon Bounty
task.content:
Join this Gibwork Developer Hackathon bounty to create a new non-web-app use case for Gibwork using the SDK, CLI, or MCP.

This bounty is focused on practical developer workflows, automations, integrations, or tooling that demonstrate a compelling way Gibwork can be used outside of traditional web applications.

Bounty Description

The selected participants will be responsible for:

  • Designing and building a new Gibwork bounty use case that uses the SDK, CLI, or MCP in a meaningful and functional way.

  • Focusing this bounty on non-web-app development, such as developer tooling, automation flows, terminal-based utilities, AI agent integrations, backend workflows, local productivity tools, or other creative bounty concepts.

  • Implementing a working prototype that clearly shows how the bounty use case works, what problem it solves, and how Gibwork is integrated.

  • Documenting the bounty solution so another developer can understand the setup, usage flow, and expected output.

  • Providing a short demo of the completed bounty build, including the core workflow and successful execution.

Requirements

  • The bounty must use Gibwork SDK, CLI, or MCP as a core part of the implementation.

  • The bounty must be a new use case, not a minor variation of an existing demo.

  • The bounty must not be a web app, frontend dashboard, or browser-based product.

  • The bounty should solve a real developer, operations, automation, research, or workflow problem with a clear practical outcome.

  • The bounty submission must include clear setup instructions, dependencies, and steps to run or test the project.

  • The submission should be functional, organized, and understandable enough for basic reviewer validation.

  • Must attend at least 2 of the hackathon sessions on Discord.

What to Submit

  • A public GitHub repository URL for the completed bounty project, including all source code and a README.

  • A short written summary in the repository README or shared document explaining the bounty use case, why it is valuable, and which Gibwork toolset was used (SDK, CLI, or MCP).

  • Setup and usage instructions for the bounty project, including installation steps, environment variables, commands to run, and sample input/output.

  • A screen recording or demo video URL showing the bounty workflow from setup or execution through successful output.

  • Screenshots of the bounty project running, such as terminal output, logs, agent interactions, or generated results.

  • Any exported deliverables produced by the bounty project, such as output files, reports, generated artifacts, or shared document links, if applicable.

How to start

  • Submit to the Google form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSejpks7hItR6zBUXpdrwgUDrwvEcmnJj6nlFbUXKIyNkVVfag/viewform?usp=dialog

  • Check Discord (https://discord.gg/2577tTsRt) to see if you have been rewarded the Hackathon role.

  • Once rewarded the Discord role you can start the work.
